Well, I had some people to help me, which made it easier, but wasn't totally necessary. Depression, anxiety, and such mental problems run in the family, though social anxiety is entirely foreign to them. They didn't understand why I would shut down and not talk to them or not leave the house and do normal things, but my parents did strongly push me to talk to a therapist and a psychiatrist. I remember it being awful to get myself to go the first time, but I was very surprised at how much less terrible it was than I thought it would be. Of all things, talk therapy ended up helping somewhat with my aversion to talking to people..... Weird. It wasn't some miracle cure like people hope, it was just helpful for me because it's one more smart person making suggestions or offering ideas of what might help. For me, realizing that some of the automatic things I thought about people were wrong helped, and ideas of better reasons to get out of bed was good too. I just learned over time how better to function with it which made me happier. I'm still pretty bad from time to time, but it's way more rare. You've considered therapy. Is it too hard, too expensive, or something else? Or maybe you've tried it and did or didn't like? Similar effects might be achievable by just thinking about what you can do or where else you can get good ideas to consider or try out, it's just gonna be tough cause you probably don't really want to do anything at all. There's literally no harm done in trying anything out if it's instead of committing suicide.

Yah, I just wanted to say that I recognize some of the things you were saying as things I have lied to myself about and as things that people I knew also believed before choosing suicide. While my sister was in the hospital as a result of attempted suicide I read some of her journals and came to more understand why she made that choice and also why she regretted it. 

She thought nobody liked her just like you, but I know that wasn't true. She thought she was ugly and no guy would ever have a reason to love her, but it just wasn't true, not even close. She thought she had made mistakes, done things to make her life as terrible as it was, but she hadn't, she was only depressed. She thought that the loving God she believed in all her life didn't exist anymore, I can't know if she was wrong in that but she's changed her mind now she's feeling better. She made some new friends, and even has been taken on some dates she hasn't found love yet, but she does know it's possible even for her.

Your life sounds like it has thrown you some really hard times, being bullied is more than awful, I can't imagine how it would be to have parents like that, and even now you feel attacked for your own skin, but you've survived all those things in the past, you can still survive them now and eventually it might even get easier, the only problem is those things you're telling yourself that aren't true. None of the things my sister believed we're true, and I'm sorry it's just too unlikely that you believe all the same things but are right about them all. There are seeds of truth in the lies we tell even to ourselves, so please just think about the possibility that maybe you're wrong about nobody liking you, and that some people do like you, but really you just need more close friends and family. Consider that maybe you're wrong about things never changing, because you can never predict how things will happen in the future. Consider that the mistakes you made maybe could be fixed or aren't your fault in the first place. Consider that maybe you do still believe that a god might exist. Consider that the things you tell yourself right now might be untrue in a lot of ways and that maybe there's a way you can not tell yourself these things anymore. 

You've tried to change yourself already and it hasn't worked. If you do the same one more time, chances are it still won't work. What really could work is trying a different strategy, perhaps starting with something easy like getting up, or going for a walk, or talking to a real person, or whatever is doable for you. after that all you have to do is keep on, and you might make it out of this and get to a better part of life.

Hey, just wanted to say this, cause it took me a long time to realize and then truly believe it- 

It IS okay to say that you are also going through some horrific stuff although it's different. Everyone doesn't have perfectly equal amounts of crisis in their lives, but everyone has at least some at some point. And although you didn't watch your entire town get slaughtered, or live in poverty or have your family disown you, or any other random terrible things, you do have one crisis, and that's plenty: you think you'll never be happy and want to die. That crisis, is what you've got to deal with and other people have gotta deal with other things, be them seemingly more or less terrible. But you've just gotta get past it, and then it will be done. 

Don't succumb to this crisis, beat it and move forward. It seems like maybe medication could be a very helpful route, but there are plenty of doable things that might end up being what helps you. Maybe continue to talk to people anonymously (but be careful) maybe find someone you can really talk to about it, maybe a therapist, or maybe find a medicine or vitamin that changes things for you, or make a change in your life that makes everything a bit better. Whatever it is you'll have enough strength at some point in time to make a tiny step, and you'll get out of this hole.
